:::{#def-schur-complement}
#### Schur complement

For a block matrix
$\matr{X} = \begin{bmatrix} \matr{A} & \matr{B} \\ \tp{\matr{B}} & \matr{C} \end{bmatrix}$
as in @thm-block-quadratic with $\matr{A}$ invertible,
the **Schur complement** of $\matr{A}$ in $\matr{X}$ is the $m \times m$ matrix
$\matr{S} = \matr{C} - \tp{\matr{B}} \matr{A}^{-1} \matr{B}$ defined in @thm-block-quadratic.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-schur-complement}
#### Schur complements of $2 \times 2$ matrices

- For $\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$ with $\matr{A} = [5]$:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \matr{S} &= 5 - 4 \cd \tfrac{1}{5} \cd 4 \\
  &= \tfrac{25}{5} - \tfrac{16}{5} \\
  &= \tfrac{9}{5},
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  that is, $\matr{S} = [\tfrac{9}{5}]$.
- For $\matr{D} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ with $\matr{A} = [1]$:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \matr{S} &= [1 - 2 \cd 1 \cd 2] \\
  &= [-3].
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- For $\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ the top-left block $[0]$ is not invertible,
  so there is no Schur complement of it.

:::
